chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who linked it up to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him):

He said: Five groups of people complete their prayers whether they are on a journey or at home: the carters, the renters of beasts of burden, the ash-Shitqan (which is the postal courier), the shepherd, and the sailor, because it is their profession.
ai.seo_question: Who are the five groups of people who do not shorten their prayers while traveling according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes a jurisprudential exception to the general rule of shortening prayers (qasr) for five specific professions—carters, beast-renters, postal couriers, shepherds, and sailors—whose work inherently involves continuous movement or travel. The ruling highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the 'nature of the work' (li-anna 'amalahum) serves as a valid justification for maintaining the complete four-rak'ah prayer, distinguishing these travelers from those who are merely passing through. This reflects the practical application of ease in worship, ensuring that those whose livelihood depends on constant transit are not burdened by the complexities of shortening prayers while on duty.
